questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiom from the options to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence. After his business failed, he had to reduce spending and adjust to a frugal lifestyle.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiom from the options to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence.

After his business failed, he had to reduce spending and adjust to a frugal lifestyle.

options.text: hit the nail on the head
options.html: hit the nail on the head

options.text: let the cat out of the bag
options.html: let the cat out of the bag

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1)

Key Points

  • The word "tighten his belt" means to reduce spending and live more frugally. (अपने खर्चों में कटौती करना)
    • Example: With the recent financial crisis, many families have had to tighten their belts.

Therefore, the correct answer "tighten his belt."

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Hit the nail on the head (सटीक बात करना): To describe exactly what is causing a situation or problem.

  • Let the cat out of the bag (राज़ खोलना): To reveal a secret or a surprise by accident.
    • Example: He let the cat out of the bag about their surprise party.
  • Kick the bucket (मर जाना): To die.
    • Example: The old man finally kicked the bucket after a long illness.

questions.question: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. The minister promised to provide free laptops to the public if his (party came in power).
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully.

The minister promised to provide free laptops to the public if his (party came in power).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • The phrase "party came in power" means that a political party has won the election and is now in control of the government. (पार्टी सत्ता में आई)
    • Example: When the party came in power, they immediately started implementing their policies.
  • "party forms the government" refers to the same situation where a political party has won the election and is now responsible for governing the country. (पार्टी सरकार बनाती है)
    • Example: If the party forms the government, they plan to introduce new educational reforms.

Hence, we can infer that the correct phrase to substitute 'party came in power' is 'party forms the government'.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: party loses the election (पार्टी चुनाव हार जाती है): This means the political party did not win the election.
    • Example: If the party loses the election, they will not be able to implement their manifesto.
  • Option 2: he loses the election (वह चुनाव हार जाता है): This means the individual candidate did not win the election.
    • Example: If he loses the election, he will not be able to serve his constituency.
  • Option 4: he comes to a party (वह एक पार्टी में आता है): This means the individual attended a social gathering.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined segment of the given sentence. In the jungle, I saw a group of lions.

questions.question: Choose the option that can substitute the underlined segment correctly and complete the meaning of the sentence. Navika is a superb and impressive child in her class.

questions.question: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'. The train left before I reached the station.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'.

The train left before I reached the station.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2'.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence describes two past events: the train leaving and the speaker reaching the station.
  • To show that the train leaving happened before the speaker reached the station, we use the past perfect tense for the earlier action. Hence, "had left" is correct.
  • The correct sentence should be: "The train had left before I reached the station."
  • Thus, "had left before I reached" is the correct substitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Anyone reading these lines will thought that the writer is very sad.

Anyone reading these lines will thought that the writer is very sad.

options.text: will think that the writer is

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is Will think that the writer is.

Key Points

  • The correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is "will think that the writer is."
  • The original sentence is in the present continuous tense ("reading"), so we need a future tense to indicate a future event.
  • "Will think" is the correct future tense to use here, as it indicates that the action (thinking) will occur in the future.
  • The other options either use the wrong tense or incorrect verb forms.
  • Option 1 uses "will have think," which is grammatically incorrect.
  • Option 2 uses "are think," which is also incorrect.
  • Option 3 uses "have thinking," which is the present perfect tense and is not appropriate for this sentence.
  • Therefore, option 4 is the most appropriate and grammatically correct option.


Correct Sentence: Anyone reading these lines will think that the writer is very sad.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. If his father will give money , he will buy a sports bike.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

If his father will give money, he will buy a sports bike.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The word "will give" implies a future action but in conditional sentences, we use the present simple tense in the if-clause to indicate a future possibility. (भविष्य की संभावना बताने के लिए 'if-clause' में वर्तमान काल का उपयोग किया जाता है।)
    • Example: If it rains, we will stay indoors.
  • "Gives" is the correct present simple tense form used in conditional sentences to indicate a future event. (वर्तमान सरल काल का सही रूप है जो भविष्य की घटना को इंगित करता है।)
    • Example: If she gives permission, we will go on the trip.
  • Hence, we can infer that the correct form is 'If his father gives money'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: No substitution (कोई प्रतिस्थापन नहीं): This option suggests that the original sentence is correct, which it is not.
    • Example: No substitution is needed when the sentence is already correct.
  • Option 2: If his father give money (अगर उसके पिता पैसा दे): Incorrect subject-verb agreement as 'father' is singular and should be followed by 'gives'.
    • Example: If he give me the keys, I will drive. (Incorrect)
  • Option 3: If his father gave money (अगर उसके पिता ने पैसा दिया): This implies a past action and does not fit the future conditional context.
    • Example: If he gave me the keys, I would drive. (Past conditional)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Peter was the last to know that she had been cheating of him .
questions.questionHtml:

Peter was the last to know that she had been cheating of him.
questions.solution:

  • The word "cheating" means acting dishonestly or unfairly in order to gain an advantage, especially in a game or examination. (धोखा देना)
    • Example: He was caught cheating during the exam.
  • "Cheating on him" refers to being unfaithful to him in a romantic relationship. (धोखा देना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Cheating in him (उसमें धोखा देना): This phrase is grammatically incorrect and does not convey a meaningful sense in English.

  • Cheat of him (उससे धोखा देना): This phrase could imply depriving him of something through deceit, but it is not the correct usage in the context of romantic unfaithfulness.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The manager complained that Sheetal's email was not up to the standard for the company.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The manager complained that Sheetal's email was not up to the standard for the company.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. "up to the mark".

Key Points

  • The word "up to the mark" means to meet the required standard or quality; satisfactory or acceptable. (मानक के अनुरूप)
    • Example: The teacher felt that the student's essay was not up to the mark and needed improvement.
  • The given phrase "up to the standard" also means meeting the required level or quality but is less commonly used in comparison to "up to the mark." (मानक के अनुरूप)
    • Example: The hotel facilities were up to the standard expected by international travelers.
  • Both phrases imply the same meaning, but "up to the mark" is more appropriate and widely used in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 2: an uphill task (दुर्लभ कार्य): Refers to a task that is very challenging or difficult to accomplish.
    • Example: Completing the project in such a short time will be an uphill task.
  • Option 3: up and doing (सक्रिय): Refers to being active and energetic in getting things done.
    • Example: After her recovery, she was up and doing, ready to tackle new challenges.
  • Option 4: under the nose (आंखों के सामने): Refers to something happening right in front of someone without them noticing.
    • Example: The thief stole the wallet under the nose of the security guard.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Last night, I failed to sleep because of some familiar issues that couldn’t be avoided.
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3)

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the word 'inevitable' is the most appropriate choice.
  • The word 'inevitable' means unavoidable, which fits the context of the sentence better than the other options.
  • The other options do not convey the same meaning. For example:
    • Unthinkable: Not capable of being imagined or grasped mentally.
    • Unsolvable: Not able to be solved.
    • Incapable: Not having the ability, qualification, or strength to perform a specified act or function.

Additional Information

  • Understanding the context of a sentence is crucial in selecting the most appropriate word.
  • It's important to consider the exact meaning and nuance of each word option.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. During the preparation for competitive exams, Meena avoided going to parties.

questions.question: In question four alternatives are given for the underlined Idiom/Phrase in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase. In life, there will be many situations where you have to choose between the devil and the deep blue sea
questions.questionHtml:

In life, there will be many situations where you have to choose between the devil and the deep blue sea

    • Example: After years of bullying others, he finally got a taste of his own medicine.

Therefore, the correct idiom for the given phrase is: a slap on the wrist.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. There was some drawing-pins in my desk.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He lived on the bank of a mighty river, broad and deep, that have always silently rolling on to a vast undiscovered ocean.
